description: Issue #957: neutralizes _DashboardController.Update's merge-on-update reconciliation by commenting out the `DashboardCredentialMasking.ReconcileWidgetHeaders(dashboard.Widgets, existing.Widgets)` call (and the BadRequest short-circuit that follows it), reintroducing the pre-#957 'wholesale replace' write. Because MaskForRead never returns a header's real value, and the shipped dashboard designer (framework_dashboard_designer.js's _readForm -- no headers-editing UI, never sends a headers key) never round-trips headers at all, this mutation reopens two distinct live defects simultaneously: (a) a caller-submitted definition that never touched a widget's headers silently WIPES them (the second defect the #957 fix addresses -- every save through the shipped designer would wipe REST widget headers), and (d)/(e) a masked sentinel value round-tripped from a prior GET (or fabricated for a header that never existed) is persisted as a LITERAL credential instead of being restored/rejected. red_tests below cover exactly those three cases against the real JsonFileDashboardService-backed controller (not a mock, so the actual persisted widget state is asserted, not just the HTTP status code). green_test is DashboardCredentialMaskingTests.ReconcileWidgetHeaders_case_a_null_headers_preserves_all_existing_headers, a pure unit test that calls DashboardCredentialMasking.ReconcileWidgetHeaders directly (never through the controller) -- it stays green because the reconciliation LOGIC itself is untouched by this mutation; only its invocation at the Update() call site was severed.
target_symbol: _DashboardController.Update(string, DashboardDefinition) -- the DashboardCredentialMasking.ReconcileWidgetHeaders(...) call, its BadRequest short-circuit, and the LogWarnings call, line ~164-166

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Dashboard.Dash: Expected object not to be <null> because a masked-sentinel value for a header that never existed must be rejected, not silently stored as a literal credential

to be "Bearer real-secret-should-never-reach-a-viewer" with a length of 46 because re-submitting the masked value the caller itself received must restore the real credential, not persist the sentinel literal, but "••••••••" has a length of 8

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured by applying the patch manually and building/running exactly as run_mutant.py does (`dotnet build -c Release` then `dotnet test -c Release --no-restore --filter <red_test_filter>`) before writing this file, then reverting the manual patch application and letting run_mutant.py apply/run/revert it itself for the actual gate run -- an earlier version of this file (before this run) had pinned DEBUG-config failure text using each assertion's CallerArgumentExpression-captured subject (e.g. 'stored!.Widgets["w1"]...'), which turned out not to match the RELEASE config's actual text (same finding as the sibling 957-dashboard-get-masking-neutralize entry -- FluentAssertions falls back to a generic type name, e.g. 'Expected dictionary not to be <null>.'/'Expected object not to be <null> because ...'/'Expected string to be ... because ...', for the subject text under Release for these three call sites). Patterns above match the STABLE (type-name-fallback-safe) portion of the three actual Release-mode messages. No other test in the same filter's TRX went red.
